Retest: Fresh scan required after host maintenance.

Finding: Backend dependency baseline contained 34 advisory records across nine packages.
Remediation / disposition: Updated FastAPI/Pydantic/SuperTokens/Motor/PyMongo/multipart/mail/AWS dependencies and removed unused python-jose.
Retest: Deployed tree reduced 34 to one advisory. Running image versions were inspected directly; 32 deployed-image tests and acceptance passed.
Status: Closed in production; one residual tracked in Q3-VA-003

Finding: cryptography 49.0.0 has PYSEC-2026-3552; fixed in 50.0.0. Current fastapi-mail 1.6.5 requires <50.
Evidence: Final pip-audit and Trivy backend image scan.
Remediation / disposition: Keep the finding visible; do not force an unsupported resolver override. Track a compatible FastAPI-Mail release or replace the mail abstraction, then upgrade and retest OTP/invitation/password-reset mail.
Retest: Final audit still reports exactly one known backend dependency finding.

Finding: Frontend production dependency audit initially returned four vulnerabilities.
Retest: Current production-branch full/production-only npm audit: 0; deployed frontend Trivy: 0; production build passed.

Finding: Production Compose stored default database credentials and a placeholder application secret in tracked configuration. A tracked value must be treated as exposed even if access is network-restricted.
Remediation / disposition: Replaced values with mandatory deployment variables, added a non-secret production template, and retained loopback-only database bindings. Existing values were moved to the untracked production environment during deployment without disclosure.
Retest: Production Compose has no tracked defaults and database bindings are loopback-only. Actual credential rotation remains pending.

Finding: Production OpenAPI schema was publicly accessible at /api/v1/openapi.json (HTTP 200).
Remediation / disposition: Disabled Swagger, ReDoc and OpenAPI when ENVIRONMENT=production; retained them in non-production environments.
Retest: Direct post-deployment public retest on 12 August returned HTTP 404.

Finding: Production backend Compose used a source bind mount and Uvicorn --reload, increasing mutable-code and development-runtime exposure.
Remediation / disposition: Removed the bind mount and reload mode; production image now runs copied code with four non-root workers.
Retest: Direct container inspection confirmed appuser, no backend mounts, four Uvicorn workers, healthy state and zero restarts.

Finding: Latest OCI CIS check 5.2.14 reports that only strong SSH MAC algorithms are not enforced.
Evidence: OCI managed scan completed before the final release: 17 pass, 1 fail.
Remediation / disposition: Direct sshd -T now shows key-only authentication and only hmac-sha2-512-etm, hmac-sha2-256-etm, and umac-128-etm; configuration syntax and a second direct SSH session passed.
Retest: Trigger/review a fresh OCI CIS scan to reconcile the managed score before closure.

Finding: The inner frontend NGINX response lacked several browser defense headers; the first deployment also exposed an NGINX add_header inheritance gap on the app shell.
Evidence: Public/inner header captures and active NGINX configuration.
Remediation / disposition: Added and deployed nosniff, SAMEORIGIN, strict-origin referrer policy and restrictive permissions policy, explicitly repeating them in the index.html location.
Retest: Commit bdb03b5, workflow 31539611417; inner and public app-shell responses now contain all four headers plus public HSTS/CSP.

Finding: SuperTokens Python SDK remediation requires CDI 5.4; core 11.0 supports only through CDI 5.3.
Evidence: Reproduced signup failure after SDK update.
Remediation / disposition: Pinned and deployed SuperTokens core 11.3.7, which supports CDI 5.4. Avoided 12.0 because direct 11.0-to-12.0 local upgrade did not migrate one schema column correctly.
Retest: Production backups passed; core 11.3.7 is running and the deployed failed-login acceptance passed.

Finding: Bandit B608 matched string interpolation in OCI Object Storage URL construction as possible SQL injection.
Remediation / disposition: Reviewed manually: the code constructs an HTTPS object URL and executes no SQL.
Retest: No SQL API or database call exists in the matched function.

Remediation / disposition: Retain as code-quality backlog; no direct exploit path was established. Add structured logging when these paths are next modified.
